recentItems.title: Ecuador fishermen caught between US drug war and criminal groups
recentItems.description:
Ecuadorian fishing communities say they are increasingly caught between drug-trafficking gangs and expanding US military operations along the Pacific coast. 
Families of missing crew members, including that of the Fiorella vessel, say they have received no answers eight months after their relatives disappeared near the Galapagos Islands. 
Others describe drone attacks, detentions and transfers abroad without due process. Ecuador, a key transit route for cocaine and close US security ally, is facing mounting criticism over accountability for such operations.

Al Jazeera’s Teresa Bo reports from Manta, Ecuador.

recentItems.title: Authorities in India rescue baby orangutans dumped in forest
recentItems.description:
Authorities have rescued five baby orangutans found abandoned in India’s Odisha forest. Officials believe they were smuggled, since the critically endangered species only live on the islands of Borneo and Sumatra.

recentItems.title: Two years of Sinaloa cartel war leave Mexico's Culiacan living in fear
recentItems.description:
Two years after fighting erupted between rival factions of Mexico's Sinaloa Cartel, violence continues to grip the state despite the deployment of 15,000 troops. Thousands have been killed or disappeared, more than 5,000 businesses have closed and 27,000 jobs lost. The conflict, pitting sons of Joaquín 'El Chapo' Guzmán against those loyal to Ismael 'El Mayo' Zambada, has also implicated the state's governor, now on leave amid US trafficking allegations.

Al Jazeera’s John Holman reports from Culiacan, Mexico.

recentItems.title: How a Himalayan avalanche unleashed a trail of destruction across Nepal
recentItems.description:
It's been two weeks since floods swept through communities in the Himalayas. When a section of Langtang Lirung mountain and the glacier above it collapsed, millions of cubic metres of rock and ice fell more than a kilometre to the valley below. The impact registered as a magnitude 5.2 earthquake. The mass of debris travelled more than 14 kilometres in seven minutes towards the China-Nepal border crossing, which was obliterated. The surge of melting ice, rock and sediment then plunged down the Trishuli valley, gathering more water and gouging chunks out of the riverbank. Workers on site filmed its approach before fleeing, but hundreds of others were buried. The avalanche swept away bridges, buildings and entire villages, carrying boulders bigger than cars. Within an hour, it had left a trail of devastation stretching more than 50 kilometres, while flooding continued south for more than 100 kilometres. 

Al Jazeera's Daniel McKerrell explains.

recentItems.title: 600-year-old tomb of pre-Incan Chimu kingdom found in Peru | AJ Shorts
recentItems.description:
Archaeologists in Peru have uncovered an almost intact Chimu funerary platform containing the remains of at least 38 people. Its main chamber had remained sealed for nearly 600 years, offering rare insight into the pre-Incan civilisation.

recentItems.title: The case for the US going back to the firing squad
recentItems.description:
The US has evolved its method of criminal executions, but drug shortages and protests over medical ethics have made lethal injections increasingly difficult to carry out. John Malcolm of the Meese Institute tells Al Jazeera that the US should ‘go back to a firing squad’.

recentItems.title: Marco Rubio visits Colombia as US seeks stronger influence in Latin America
recentItems.description:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has been visiting Colombia — the first stop on a tour of three South American nations, that have recently aligned with the Trump administration.
Rubio promised a stronger relationship with Colombia, following four years of tension under the country's previous left-wing government.

Al Jazeera’s Alessandro Rampietti reports from the coastal city of Barranquilla.
